claim_scope: Authoritative post-observation was mapped to the frozen typed revalidation state on every confirmatory antecedent.

For REVISED feedback in the same frozen relation scope, exposing correctly bound feedback changed both later participation and later realized selection relative to record-only in all three confirmatory observation families.
CONFIRMED and INCONCLUSIVE feedback did not perturb the later F1-vs-F2 decision path in the frozen matrix.
REVISED feedback did not act as a permanent/global exclusion when the frozen recurrence scope shifted.
Permuting the exposed state while preserving stored provenance demonstrates that state content, not mere feedback existence, can alter later governance behavior in the controlled harness.
limitations: Finite synthetic confirmatory matrix; not a real-world or CARLA generalization claim.
Newly committed Completed Experience reuse was deliberately disabled, so this experiment isolates revalidation feedback rather than accumulated CE reuse.
The outcome-to-state mapping is a frozen directional experimental contract, not a learned universal outcome evaluator.
No aggregate winner score and no claim of general system superiority.
